Eissler: Herr Professor, I would very much like to know everything you are willing to tell about Freud. There may be some delicate matters! I am quite happy to leave the room.

Jung: I'm old now and I simply cannot get used to these contraptions. I mean, you look at the blasted thing and what it does, you see. I hate broadcasting, and all of that, isn't that so?! I find it utterly repugnant, to the very last fiber!

Eissler: If I were younger, I could go home and write down what you've told me. But my memory is not so good.

Jung: Well, of course! Once you've lost not only your feet but your memory as well! Yes, good Lord, I could write a book about what I experienced with Freud! But how does one say that in a few words? Freud was an exceedingly complex phenomenon. A very interesting man, with very many bright sides and dark sides.

Eissler: Is there such a thing as indiscretion in history?
